subject: Weekly MAP sync — SDK/Auth/Streaming task tracker
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Weber <sam.weber@integracom.com>, Priya Desai <p.desai@integracom.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly MAP sync — SDK/Auth/Streaming task tracker

Hi Sam / Priya,

Quick weekly checkpoint on the MAP and integration items we committed to during last week's runbook review. I attached the latest MAP workbook (Integracom_MAP_v1.2.xlsx) with the task tracker tab updated. High-level status below — call out any corrections and we'll push updates into the tracker.

Summary (high level)
- SDK integration: in-progress. Initial client PR ready; packaging/CI tweaks pending. (owner: Monica)
- Auth: token rotation + scoped keys plan drafted; need final sign-off on TTLs. (owner: Sean)
- Streaming / chunking: prototype works for short sessions; need to validate long-running tool-calling sessions. (owner: Grace)

Action items (short):
1) Monica — finalize SDK CI pipelines and publish v0.9.1 to test registry. Due: 2026-09-03.
2) Sean — confirm HMAC key rotation window + update auth-checklist PDF for Integracom. Due: 2026-09-01.
3) Grace — run long-session streaming soak on staging (24h) and report token/KV cache behavior. Due: 2026-09-06.
4) Karthik (me) — coordinate canary rollout plan and update the MAP with rollback gating. Due: 2026-09-07.

Notes / risks:
- Streaming: observed memory growth in one workload when tool-calling with repeated stateful steps; Grace to instrument KV cache and share traces.
- Auth: Integracom requested shorter TTLs for service keys. This may impact SDK refresh logic — Sean to propose options (refresh-before-expiry vs background refresh).
- Timeline: Integracom Q3 close target (formal acceptance) still looks achievable if SDK CI and auth sign-off complete next week.

Attachments: Integracom_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (task tracker), auth-integration-checklist.pdf (draft)

Proposed sync: same time Thursday 10:00am PT — short 30m to finalize go/no-go checklist. If that works for you, I'll send the invite.

Regards,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Partnerships & Integrations
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Sam Weber <sam.weber@integracom.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <p.desai@integracom.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP sync — SDK/Auth/Streaming task tracker

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- For streaming: our primary concern is the tool-calling pattern where session state grows for ~2–3 hours (we run inference in a conversational loop). If memory growth is expected at that length, we need mitigation before canary. Can Grace share expected memory profile thresholds?

- Auth TTLs: security prefers the shorter TTL option (15m) but we understand that will increase refresh traffic. Can Sean quantify the expected refresh QPS for 1k concurrent sessions? That number will drive whether we implement background refresh in the SDK or rely on short-lived service tokens with a broker.

- Quick ask: can you add a small column in the MAP tracker for "blocking (Y/N)" so we can quickly see go/no-go items?

We'll plan to make Thursday 10:00am PT work for the team. Priya and I will join.

Best,

Sam Weber
Head of Platform Integrations
Integracom
sam.weber@integracom.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP sync — SDK/Auth/Streaming task tracker

Sam — thanks, good asks. Quick updates on SDK side:

- CI / packaging: PR is open (link in tracker). The test registry has v0.9.1 candidate; packaging issue found with Windows wheel metadata — will be fixed today.
- Background refresh: implementing a refresh-before-expiry hook is fast for the JS + Python SDKs; I can have a prototype by Wed (2026-09-02). If Sean's QPS estimate pushes traffic higher, we can gate JS to background-refresh and leave Python to on-demand, but that is just a fallback.

I've added a "blocking" column in Integracom_MAP_v1.2.xlsx and marked Auth TTL and Streaming soak as blocking for canary. Please review.

Action updates (from tracker)
- Monica: SDK CI fixes + publish v0.9.1 -> 2026-09-03 (In progress)
- Sean: Auth QPS estimate + updated checklist -> 2026-09-01 (Pending)
- Grace: Streaming soak + trace dump -> 2026-09-06 (Queued)

Grace, I can pair with you on instrumentation if you want — I can also add test clients for the longer session pattern Sam described.

—Monica
